summary: app.py has three insecure settings: Flask debug mode on while bound to all interfaces, TLS verification off on a payments call that carries a bearer token, and wildcard CORS with credentials allowed. config.py has no insecure settings for this step. I did not read README.md, package.json or requirements.txt.

findings.title: Flask debug mode enabled on all interfaces
findings.evidence: app.run(host="0.0.0.0", port=8080, debug=True) exposes the Werkzeug debugger, which allows code execution, on every interface
findings.recommendation: Remove debug=True and run behind a production WSGI server. Control debug through the environment, and bind to 127.0.0.1 or a reverse proxy.

findings.title: TLS verification disabled on payments call carrying bearer token
findings.evidence: requests.post(..., headers={"Authorization": Bearer ...}, verify=False) sends customer data and a credential without certificate checks
findings.recommendation: Remove verify=False so certificates are verified. If a private CA is needed, point verify at its CA bundle.

findings.title: Wildcard CORS with credentials allowed
findings.evidence: Access-Control-Allow-Origin set to "*" and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials set to "true" (line 19) in after_request for all responses
findings.recommendation: Restrict the allowed origins to an explicit allowlist of dashboard origins. Do not combine a wildcard origin with credentials.

limitations: README.md, package.json and requirements.txt were not read.
The service has no Dockerfile or deployment files to check for container settings.
